author: Mark Atwood
text:
Investigation done; the bead's framing of option (b) is wrong in light of a workspace pattern I found, so this needs a human call between option (a) and a revised (b').

Findings from read-only inspection:

1. JsContactId is used at exactly ONE site: Title.organization_id (lib.rs:338). No other use in this crate or any sibling.

2. RFC 9553 has exactly ONE scalar Id-typed reference: Title.organizationId (RFC 9553 §2.2.5 / table line 3012). Every other Id appears as the key type of an Id[X] map. The bead description is accurate about that.

3. The bead's option (b) — "apply JsContactId to SpeakToAs.pronouns keys" — conflicts with the Sloppy-Value pattern in jmap-contacts-types. That crate's deserializers (lib.rs:705-993) decode every one of RFC 9553's ~16 Card-level Id[X] maps as HashMap<String, X>, not HashMap<JsContactId, X>. Applying JsContactId to one map-key site here while the consumer crate uses String everywhere would be a workspace-wide inconsistency. The original framing of (b) is therefore not a viable target.

The live options are:

  (a) DROP JsContactId entirely. Title.organization_id becomes Option<String>. This makes sgrr.13 (Display/FromStr), sgrr.23 (validate helper), and sgrr.25 (redundant non_exhaustive) all moot. Aligns with the consumer crate's existing String-keyed map pattern. Loses the type-safety signal on the one scalar Id field.

  (b') KEEP JsContactId, document the policy as "scalar Id references only, not map keys" in lib.rs:55-63 rustdoc and PLAN.md. Add a clarifying note to SpeakToAs.pronouns doc-comment that the key is a JSContact Id but typed as String per workspace policy. Leaves sgrr.13/.23/.25 as valid follow-ups.

Recommendation: option (a). Rationale:
  - JsContactId carries no validation today (sgrr.23), no Display/FromStr/Into (sgrr.13), and #[non_exhaustive] on a private-field newtype is redundant (sgrr.25). The type is decorative.
  - One usage site is too thin a justification for a newtype that introduces three follow-up beads worth of maintenance burden.
  - The Sloppy-Value pattern in jmap-contacts-types is already the de-facto workspace policy: Id-keyed maps use String. Dropping JsContactId makes the policy "all JSContact Id references use String" — single rule, no exceptions.
  - This is a pre-publish decision; the crate is unpublished so the breaking-change cost is zero.

If you prefer (b'), the PLAN.md addition would say:
  "JSContact Id references typed JsContactId where they appear as scalar
   values in wire fields (per RFC 9553's only such site, Title.organizationId).
   When an Id appears as a map key per RFC 9553 Id[X] notation, the key
   stays bare String to match the workspace Sloppy-Value pattern used by
   the consuming jmap-contacts-types crate."

Either decision unblocks me to either remove JsContactId + its 4 trait impls + the test at lib.rs:1557, OR add the doc + PLAN.md edits and close .13/.23/.25 accordingly.
